parties:
Mustafa Kamal and others   -------- Petitioners [WP No. 207 of 1986)
Sebera Begum   -------- Petitioner [WP No. 208 of 1986)
Vs.
Director of Land Records and others  -------- .Respondents [In both the WPs]
full_judgment:
Qazi Shafiuddin, J.: This Rule Nisi issued in Writ Petition No. 207 of 1986 has been directed against the impugned order dated 31.3.1986 (Annexure E) passed by the Respondent No. 1 while the Rule in Writ Petition No. 208 of 1986 is directed against the impugned order dated 31.3.1986 (Annexure G to the petition) calling upon the respondents to show cause why the same should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

2. Since identical question of facts as well as law having been involved in these two Rules the same are being heard and will now be disposed of by this judgment.

3. The petitioner's case in Writ Petition No. 207/86 is that they purchased the land in question from one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 15.8.79. Originally the land was recorded in the name of its owner Abdur Rahman in RS khatian. Subsequently Fazar Rahman, the heir of Abdur Rahman, sold the same to one Nur Mohammad by registered deed of sale and Nur Mohammad sold the same in favour of one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 3.12.69. The present petitioners purchased the suit land from the said Siddique Ahmed. The petitioners claim that the suit land be recorded in their names. That one Mohammad Harunur Rashid filed an objection under section 19(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in objection Case No. 139 dated 15.10.1980 objecting the entry of the name of the respondent No.2 in the draft record of rights. The objection was not allowed.

4. Being aggrieved the petitioners and others filed an appeal case against his objection Case No. 139 dated 15.10.1980. The appeal case was numbered as Appeal case No. 25187/81. The appellate authority after complying with the due formalities and after obtaining the Survey Report and hearing the parties allowed the appeal and directed the inclusion of the names of the petitioners to the extent of 7 annas share in the draft record of rights. Thereafter a Review petition was filed by the respondent No. 2 against the order of the Appellate Authority dated 16.9.1984. The said petition was heard and disposed of by the appellate authority by rejecting the same and maintained the order passed by him in the appeal. The respondent No.2 finding no alternative filed a Second Review petition before the Director of Land Records against the order of the appellate authority dated 16.9.1984. The Director of Land Records by his order dated 31.3.1986 allowed the Second Review petition setting aside the order dated 16.9.1984 passed by the appellate authority and sent back the case to one Mr. Bazlur Rahman for hearing of the appeal afresh. Against this very order of the Director of Land Records dated 31.3.1986, the petitioners have filed this Writ Petition and obtained the present Rule.

5. The case of the respondent No.2, as it appears, is that respondent No.2 purchased 12 annas interest from Fazar Rahman the heirs of Hafizur Rahman by a registered Kabala dated 29.11.1976 and subsequently the respondent No.2 also purchased the share of Mofizur Rahman by a registered Kabala dated 2.6.80 and accordingly his name in the draft record of rights has been correctly recorded.

6. In Writ Petition No. 208 of 1986 the case of the petitioner Mosammat Sabera Begum is that one Bujarat was instituted by the respondent Nos. 2-3 impleading the petitioner as the second party before the Revenue Authority. The case was disposed of ex parte by order dated 23.6.77 wherein the name of the petitioner in the khatian was directed to be struck off and those of respondent Nos. 2-5 were to be recorded. Against the said order the petitioner filed objection case impleading the respondent Nos. 2-5 as opposite parties. The Revenue Officer considered the objection and disposed of the case by his order dated 31.5.79 maintaining the order recording the name of the respondents passed in the Biujarat dispute case. It is the case of the petitioner that the original owner of the case land was one Abdur Rahman and his name appeared in the RS khatian in Korfa right The said RS khatian was under khatian No. 25 of Jote No. 1 and the owner of the said jote No. 1 was one Abdul Aziz Sarang in raiyati right. The said Jotedar having defaulted in payment of revenue, the Jote was put to auction and ultimately the entire lands vested in the Government. One Abdus Salam prayed for re-settlement of the case land and his prayer was allowed and accordingly he became tenant directly under the Government Abdus Salam also defaulted in payment of rent and a Certificate case was started being Certificate Case No. 357 of 1945-46. The land in question was auction sold to one Ahmedur Rahman on 16.7.1946 and the sale was confirmed on 16.9.1946 and possession was delivered on 18.1.1948. The said Ahmedur Rahman got his name mutated in the RS khatian. The said auction purchaser while in possession sold the land to the petitioner by a registered kabala being kabala No. 4245 dated 21.6.1960 and since then she has been in possession of the case lands. The petitioner's name has been duly recorded in the SA khatian which has been finally published. The petitioner's name was also correctly recorded in the present khatian as per his title and possession. After the Field Survey the present respondent Nos. 5 filed a dispute case and managed to get their names recorded by suppressing notices.

7. The case of the respondent that the land originally belonged to one Abdur Rahman to the extent of 16 annas share and RS khatian No. 30/1 has been finally published in the name of the said Abdur Rahman. On his death, the respondent Nos. 2-5 were in possession of the case land as his heirs. That while in such possession they sold the land in favour of Jalalabad Housing Society and delivered possession to the said Society. As against the order the petitioner filed an appeal to the Revenue Authority and the case was registered as Appeal Case No. 23994/80. The Appellate Authority by its order dated 16.9.84 allowed the appeal and directed the recording of the name of the petitioner in the khatian by striking out the names of the respondents. Thereafter the respondent Nos. 2-5 filed a Review petition on 14.10.84 before the said appellate authority and the appellate authority heard the matter and considered the case rejecting the Review petition and maintained his earlier decision by order dated 16.9.84. That thereafter the respondent Nos. 2-5 filed a second appellation for review of the order dated 16.9.84 before the Director of Land Records. The Director of Land Records by the impugned order dated 31.3.86 allowed the second review petition of the respondents by setting aside the order dated 16.9.84 passed by the appellate authority.

8. Mr. MH Khondker, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in both the Rules, has submitted that the order dated 16.9.84 in Appeal Case No. 25187/81 having already been reviewed by the learned Appellate officer by his judgment and order dated 27.3.1985, the entertainment of a review petition and of passing the order by the Director of Land Records in reviewing the earlier order of the appeal for the second time is absolutely without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. Mr. Khandker argued that the Director of Land Records has not been vested with any statutory power to entertain and dispose of any review petition and as such his order is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and the same is of no legal effect.

9. Mr. SC Das, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submitted that the Director of Land Records has been vested with full powers and authority to revise any order passed by any Revenue Officer under Rule 44 read with Rule 43 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and as such committed no error of law.

10. We have heard the learned Advocates and perused the petition and affidavit filed by the respective parties. The only question that has cropped up in these two Rules is whether the Director of Land Records has been empowered under the statute to entertain and review any order passed by the appellate authority.

11. Under section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the Revenue Officer shall publish a draft of the record-of-rights so prepared or revised in the prescribed manner and shall receive and consider any objections relating to any entry therein during the period of such publication. By sub-section 2 of section 19 the forum for appeal is created and any aggrieved person by the order of the Revenue-Officer on any objection made under sub-section (1) of section 19 may appeal to the prescribed Revenue Authority not below the rank of an Assistant Settlement Officer in the manner and within such period as prescribed.

12. The petitioner in Writ Petition No. 207 of 1986 filed an appeal being Appeal case No. 25187/81 against the objection order passed in objection case No. 139 dated 15.10.80. The Appellate Authority by his order dated 16.9.84 allowed the appeal and directed the inclusion of the names of the petitioners to the extent of 7 annas share in the draft of record of rights.

13. It appears that the respondent No.2 filed a Review petition before the appellate authority who by his order dated 27.3.85 rejected the same and maintained the earlier order dated 16.9.84 passed in the appeal. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 moved the Director General of Land Records respondent No. 1 in a second Review. The Director General of Land Records by the impugned order dated 31.3.86 allowed the second review petition by setting aside the order dated 16.9.84 of the appellate authority directing fresh hearing by one Mr. Bazlur Rahman, an Appeal officer. The Director General appears to have exercised his powers under Rule 44 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules 1955 and caused interference under Rule 42 of the said Rules by holding that he had powers to correct, modify or set aside any record of rights made or passed in any proceeding following Rule Nos. 28-32 of the said rules.

14. Let us have a look at Rule 44 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 which reads as follows:

Powers vested in Director of Land Records and Surveys: "In respect of all operations under Chapter XVII of the Act Which have been placed under the administrative control of the Director of Land Records and Surveys. East Pakistan, he may discharge all the functions of a Revenue-Officer under the said Chapter and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under rules 36, 38, 39, 40, 41,42, 42A and 42B,"

15. Chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 deals with maintenance of the Record-of-Rights. Section 143 of the said Act runs as follows:

"The Collector shall maintain up to date, in the prescribed manner, the Record-of-rights prepared or revised under Part IV, or under this Part by correcting clerical mistake and by incorporating therein the changes on account of:

(a) the mutation of names as a result of transfer or inheritance:

(b) the subdivision, amalgamation or consolidation of holdings.

(c) the new settlement of lands or of holdings purchased by the Government, and

(d) the abatement of rent on account of abandonment or diluvian or acquisition of land."

This matter has been placed under the Director of Land Records in his Administrative Control.

16. Rule 36 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1951 speaks of Grant and Revision of certificate under section 20(4) which reads as follows:

"The authority for granting a certificate under sub-section (4) of section 20 shall be the Collector of the District, and a certificate so granted shall be subject to revision annually unless the Provincial Government by a special order otherwise directs in a particular case or class of cases."

Rule 38 speaks about Revision of record- of-rights under section 31 and Rule 39 deals with powers vested in Settlement and Assistant Settlement Officers and 40 deals with further power vested in Assistant Settlement Officer under Bengal Act V of 1875 and rule 41 empowers the Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' is also hereby vested with all the powers of superintendence of Survey under the Bengal Survey Act of 1875; Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules reads as follows:

Special power of Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of Settlement Officer:

"A Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' may at any time before the publication of final record-of-rights, direct that any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28-32 in respect of any district, part of district or local area shall be cancelled and that the proceedings shall be taken up fresh from such stage as he may direct" From the aforesaid Rules it appears that the Director General of Land Records is vested with administrative control in respect of all operation under Chapter XVII of the Act and he may discharge all the functions of a Revenue Officer and shall have powers of a Settlement Officer under Rules 36, 38, 39, 42B as such the Director General of Land Records can be said to have at best co-equal powers with that of any Revenue Officer or Settlement Officer with regard to their powers whether they are designated as Additional Designation of Settlement Officer or not but this does not mean that the Director of Land Records has been vested with superior powers to sit over their orders or decisions and to annul the same. In a quasi judicial proceedings like the present one all that is competent to do is that he may exercise any of such powers as is vested in a Revenue or Settlement Officer under Rules 44 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 in respect of a proceeding which has not attained finality, in either words, in a fresh proceeding the Director General is quite competent to assume his jurisdiction and dispose of the matter which is co-extensive with that of the Revenue or Settlement Officer. But in a matter which has already been disposed of by the Revenue Officer, namely Settlement Officer or Assistant Settlement Officer, in our view the Director of Land Records is incompetent and absolutely without power to lay his hands over such matters.

<u>17. In the present cases the Director General of Land Records has interfered with the decisions of the appellate Court which has been done under sub-section 2 of section 19. But in administrative matter under chapter 17 of the Act he has been placed in superior position in matters of control, management of Record of Rights as vested under Rule 44 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Rules.</u>

<u>The Respondent No. 1 Director General of Land Records Bangladesh has exceeded his power in entertaining and disposing of the second review petitions reviewing the orders passed by the Settlement Officer in appellate jurisdiction and as such his actions cannot but be said to be without jurisdiction. The Rule 19(1) and 19(2) has vested a power to the Settlement Officer to entertain and hear an appeal arising out of any disputed proceeding and no further power has been provided by way of revision. Although the Code of Civil Procedure has allowed an appellate authority to review any decision but no second review is contemplated under the Rule ref. by any third party namely, the Director of Land Records. Sub-section 3 of section 19 has clearly stated that when all such objections and appeals have been considered and disposed of according to such Rules, the Revenue-Officer shall finally frame the record and shall cause record to be finally published in the prescribed manner and the publication shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under this Chapter. So after the forum of appeal being exhausted, the only course left open to the Revenue Officer is to finally frame the record and such record be published in the prescribed manner. So this Rule also does not speak of any forum created for hearing a second review petition as the respondent No. 1 has entertained and disposed of. Since the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950 and the Rules made thereunder do not specifically confer on the Director of Land Records any power to revise the order passed in appeal, in our view, the impugned orders dated 31.3.86 Annexure E in Writ Petition No. 207 and 'G' in Writ Petition No. 208 of 1986 are illegal and void and as such are hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and the same are of no legal effect.</u>

In the result, both the Rules are made absolute without costs.

End.
